name: Accounting
blurb: Transaction classification, audit anomaly detection, close automation, and the shift from sampling to full-population testing, with AICPA, IMA, and benchmark sources.

points.desc: The AICPA's AI resource line covers audit use, risk, and the assurance questions the profession is settling.
points.name: AICPA maintains the professional guidance

points.desc: Census BTOS reports professional-services AI use directly from firms.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The accounting profession's body tracks technology adoption and issues the guidance on automation and AI in audit and corporate finance.
points.name: AICPA-CIMA sets the profession's direction

points.desc: The Institute of Management Accountants publishes research on AI implementation inside corporate finance and CFO organizations.
points.name: IMA covers the controller's office

points.desc: Independent model evaluation on corporate finance and tax tasks - measured accuracy rather than vendor claims.
points.name: Vals AI benchmarks financial reasoning

points.desc: MindBridge and similar audit platforms score every general-ledger entry rather than a sample - the structural change AI brings to audit is population testing replacing sampling.
points.name: Anomaly detection reaches the whole ledger

summary: Transaction classification, anomaly detection in audit, and close automation are the working uses.
